page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.26xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by the x86_64 architecture using Intel Xeon 8269CY processors clocked at 2.5 GHz. The virtual machine delivers 104 dedicated vCPUs coupled with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation ratio of 1.85 GB of RAM per vCPU. Virtualization is handled via the KVM hypervisor. The instance is designed for high core density and does not feature graphics processing units or hardware accelerators.

Network performance is backed by a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth interface. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring the configuration of external block storage volumes for system disks and persistent data persistence. This storage architecture isolates compute execution from persistent disk capacity.

The hardware configuration provides high compute throughput per resource allocation, avoiding the cost overhead of excess memory capacity or bundled high-capacity local drives. It is suitable for parallel batch workloads, software compilation, continuous integration pipelines, video transcoding, and compute-bound simulation jobs.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.26xlarge is a high-density, compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by Intel Xeon 8269CY processors running at 2.5 GHz. Managed under a KVM hypervisor, the server provides 104 dedicated vCPUs and 192.0 GB of RAM, offering a memory-to-vCPU ratio of roughly 1.85 GB per core. The instance includes a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile and contains zero GPUs. Because it lacks onboard local storage, persistent disk operations rely entirely on external cloud block storage attachments. The allocation strategy optimizes processor density for parallel computation without allocating excessive memory capacity. This design yields cost-effective multi-threaded execution for compute-intensive workloads that require massive vCPU throughput, such as large-scale build and compilation systems, continuous integration servers, video encoding pipelines, batch data processing, and distributed simulation environments.
